dedupe_keys.name: bikeshare and subway ridership changes during the covid 19 pandemic in new york city

description: This study by H. Wang and R. B. Noland, published in Transport Policy in 2021, examines how the COVID-19 pandemic affected the Citi Bike bikeshare system and the New York City subway, as New York was especially hard hit in March and April 2020 and a mandatory stay-at-home order closed all but essential businesses. Coverage: usage patterns during the lockdown compared with corresponding days in 2019, controlling for weather, through the lockdown and the reopening of economic activity up to the end of September 2020. Both subway ridership and bikeshare use plummeted at first; bikeshare use nearly returned to normal while subway ridership remained well below pre-COVID levels. The authors conclude that bikeshare gives the transport system resilience during disasters when public transit is seen as dangerous or is disrupted. Format and access: a journal article with a PubMed Central record. Licence and cost: free to read on PubMed Central; no licence stated in the record read. Caveats: one city and one kind of disruption; the abstract was the part read. The observed substitution between modes can set bikeshare fallback capacity in multimodal transit resilience models. It relates to Citi Bike system data and MTA open data in the catalogue.
